title_aliases: Overheidsingrijpen, volkomen concurrentie en internationale handel
migration_aid: migration-live-v5-to-v2.csv is newly prepared against live v5, not the historical v1-to-v2 attachment or target equivalence proof.

paragraphs.title: Belastingen: wig en nieuw evenwicht
paragraphs.intended_learning: Distinguish the price paid by buyers from the amount received by sellers; represent a per-unit tax and calculate the new traded quantity.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve linear equilibrium and substitution from §§1.3.2-1.3.3. The two-price interpretation and tax wedge are new formal learning.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: From a short market case, identify the original equilibrium, introduce the tax, calculate buyer price, seller receipt and transactions, and interpret the wedge.
paragraphs.boundary: State who remits the tax, its unit, and the competitive model assumptions. Remittance is not the same as economic tax burden. Do not add welfare accounting before §3.1.2.

paragraphs.title: Belastingdruk en welvaartsverlies
paragraphs.intended_learning: Calculate the division of the tax burden, tax revenue and welfare consequences; explain the effect of relative responsiveness.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve §3.1.1, Book 2 elasticity interpretation and surplus-area calculations. Qualitative supply responsiveness does not require introducing a new supply-elasticity formula.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Use one tax case to allocate the burden, calculate government revenue and relevant surplus changes, and explain one distributional claim from the evidence.
paragraphs.boundary: Government revenue is a transfer, not the deadweight loss. The initial welfare benchmark excludes external effects; corrective taxation returns in §4.2.4. Do not infer elasticity merely from slopes plotted with different scales.

paragraphs.title: Subsidies
paragraphs.intended_learning: Represent a per-unit subsidy, calculate both prices and transactions, and identify government expenditure and distributional effects.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Reuse the tax-wedge method with the direction reversed, and retrieve surplus calculations. Explicitly compare what changes and what stays the same.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Calculate a subsidy outcome and government expenditure, identify beneficiaries, and qualify a claim that a subsidy must increase welfare.
paragraphs.boundary: Specify the eligible transaction and payment recipient. In this first treatment assume no external benefit; §4.2.5 deliberately changes that assumption. A subsidy is not automatically an efficiency improvement.

paragraphs.title: Maximumprijs
paragraphs.intended_learning: Distinguish binding and non-binding price ceilings; calculate demand, supply, actual transactions and shortage.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve equilibrium and quantity-at-price calculations. Reuse surplus areas only after the transaction and allocation rules have been specified.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Analyse a regulated-price case, determine whether the ceiling binds, calculate the shortage and actual sales, and explain who may fail to obtain the product.
paragraphs.boundary: A low quoted price does not mean everyone buys at that price. Welfare-area calculations require an explicit allocation assumption. Avoid turning this into a full housing-policy chapter.

paragraphs.title: Minimumprijs en quota
paragraphs.intended_learning: Analyse a binding price floor and distinguish it from a production quota. Calculate surplus supply and, when specified, public purchases.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Transfer the ceiling procedure; reuse government-expenditure rectangles and the distinction between offered and actually traded quantities.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Use one supported-price case with an explicit purchase rule, then a bounded quota comparison. Calculate the quantities and budget consequences actually asked for.
paragraphs.boundary: A production quota is not automatically a price floor; a floor does not imply public purchases unless the source says so. This is a high-load paragraph: the quota comparison stays bounded. Prepares the import-quota comparison in §3.3.3 and the later minimum-wage application in §4.3.4.

paragraphs.title: Gemengde opgaven: overheidsingrijpen
paragraphs.intended_learning: Select the appropriate intervention model and integrate price, quantity, budget and welfare reasoning without new theory.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Interleave §§3.1.1-3.1.5 with Book 2 elasticity and surplus. Require method selection rather than identifying the method in every question heading.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Use a small set of contrasting policy cases. At least one target combines a numerical outcome, a labelled diagram and a source-based policy conclusion.
paragraphs.boundary: No new intervention or externality model. Do not force every intervention into one unwieldy target or one 55-minute compulsory route.

paragraphs.title: Volkomen concurrentie: kenmerken
paragraphs.intended_learning: Explain price taking and connect the market price to the individual firm’s GO and MO.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve market equilibrium and TO = P x Q; re-use the distinction between total, average and marginal revenue.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Read a market graph, transfer the price to a firm graph and explain why the firm cannot profitably choose any price it likes.
paragraphs.boundary: Explain the stated competitive assumptions. A horizontal firm demand curve is not the same as a horizontal market demand curve.

paragraphs.title: Winstmaximalisatie bij volkomen concurrentie
paragraphs.intended_learning: Use marginal comparison to select output and calculate total profit, linking MO, MK, price and average total cost.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve Book 2 cost/revenue calculations and marginal meaning. Explicitly teach the optimisation rule; do not label it revision.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Obtain the relevant marginal relation, determine the profit-maximising feasible output, calculate profit and interpret the result in a firm diagram.
paragraphs.boundary: If a quadratic total-cost function is used, teach the limited quadratic-to-linear derivative operation within this paragraph rather than assuming prior calculus. Check the direction of marginal comparisons and production capacity; MO = MK alone is not a universal maximum proof. Flag the combined mathematical and economic load for target/timing review.

paragraphs.title: Langetermijnevenwicht
paragraphs.intended_learning: Explain how entry or exit changes market supply, price and firm profit, and interpret the competitive long-run outcome.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve §3.2.2, market supply shifts, GTK and break-even. Re-use calculations to support the adjustment narrative.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Start from profit or loss, explain entry or exit, draw the direction of adjustment and identify the resulting firm outcome under the stated assumptions.
paragraphs.boundary: The familiar zero-economic-profit result requires the specified competitive entry/exit and cost assumptions. It does not mean entrepreneurs receive no remuneration or that total revenue is zero.

paragraphs.title: Gemengde opgaven: volkomen concurrentie
paragraphs.intended_learning: Integrate market price formation, firm output, profit and long-run adjustment.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Interleave Book 2 total/average/marginal distinctions, equilibrium, and §§3.2.1-3.2.3.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: A market change leads to a new firm calculation and an explanation of subsequent entry or exit; students connect market and firm evidence.
paragraphs.boundary: No monopoly or new long-run cost theory. Monopoly is taught next book, in Chapter 4.1; it is not a prerequisite for the trade chapter that follows here. A multi-stage exercise still requires an explicit initial situation and adjustment horizon.

paragraphs.title: Waarom landen handelen: specialisatie en concurrentiepositie
paragraphs.intended_learning: Explain specialisation, absolute versus comparative advantage and possible mutual gains qualitatively. Distinguish an explanation of relative opportunity cost from a general claim about a country's production strengths or competitiveness.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve scarcity, choice and the meaning of opportunity cost from Book 1. Introduce import/export and the new comparative-advantage meaning explicitly. Keep discussion of productivity, quality or costs qualitative and supported by information in the source; no formal labour-cost formula is assumed.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Use a short qualitative two-country case, including one in which the same country is more productive in both activities. Explain why relative advantage matters and how exchange may benefit both. Assess a short claim that cheaper production or greater productivity necessarily makes every participant better off. Require a reasoned answer, not a numerical specialisation table.
paragraphs.boundary: No calculated opportunity-cost ratios, production-possibility-frontier optimisation, exchange-ratio bounds or separate ruilvoet calculation objective. Do not equate absolute with comparative advantage or claim that all groups necessarily gain. The conceptual/no-calculation boundary follows the owner's retained design instruction; this revision makes no new CE/SE validation claim. Formal productivity and unit-labour-cost analysis is deferred to §4.3.1.

paragraphs.title: Wereldmarktprijs, import, export en welvaart
paragraphs.intended_learning: Explain how a stated world price changes domestic production and consumption; identify whether the country imports or exports; calculate the trade gap and interpret the effects on domestic buyers and sellers.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Reuse reading a demand/supply graph, determining quantity at a stated price, and the meaning of consumer/producer surplus. The new distinction is between domestic production, domestic consumption and the foreign trade flow, not a new equation-solving system.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Provide a labelled domestic market graph or a short table and a world price. Read or calculate domestic supply and demand, determine the import/export gap, and explain a buyer and seller outcome with evidence. Ask one qualitative surplus/distribution question. Include the reversed-price/export case in accessible practice without a second long calculation chain.
paragraphs.boundary: State a small, price-taking country, competitive markets, sufficient foreign supply/demand and the relevant transport/tariff assumptions. Keep currencies fixed. Domestic demand is not domestic production. A rise in the stated total-surplus measure is not evidence that every group gains. The target need not produce a full welfare-area ledger or balance-of-payments account.

paragraphs.title: Protectionisme: invoerheffingen en importquota
paragraphs.intended_learning: Explain why a government might restrict imports and distinguish its stated aim from effects on different groups. Use the familiar market model to interpret a per-unit import tariff; calculate remaining imports and tariff revenue in a simple case. Contrast an import quota qualitatively.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Reuse §3.3.2's world-price model and Chapter 3.1's tax, government-budget and quota concepts. Explicitly distinguish a tariff on imported units from a tax on all domestic sales.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Present one short policy source and a supplied before/after graph or quantity table. Determine the remaining imported quantity and tariff receipts, then explain effects on domestic consumers and producers. Evaluate one bounded argument for the policy. Use a short non-calculation contrast to explain why a quota need not create the same government revenue.
paragraphs.boundary: Use imported quantity, not all domestic sales, for tariff revenue. Teach the no-import boundary using graph reading or a supplied contrast; do not mechanically impose world price plus tariff after imports disappear. State the model assumptions behind the case. Quantitative quota rents/allocation, export-subsidy models, exchange-rate adjustment and formal strategic retaliation remain deferred. An industry-gain claim is not automatically an economy-wide welfare claim.

paragraphs.title: Gemengde opgaven: internationale handel
paragraphs.intended_learning: Select and combine qualitative trade explanation, familiar world-price interpretation, a short import/tariff calculation and a source-supported conclusion. Distinguish aggregate and distributional claims.
paragraphs.retrieval_and_transfer: Retrieve §§3.3.1-3.3.3 and already-taught market, budget and surplus meanings. No monopoly or labour-market procedure is needed. A source may mention jobs in ordinary language, but must not require labour-demand equations, participation statistics or unit-labour-cost calculations.
paragraphs.proposed_target_brief: Use one compact trade-policy case plus a short contrasting claim. Students select the relevant evidence, complete one manageable numerical chain from familiar graph/table data, explain effects on different groups and give a qualified conclusion. Comparative-advantage reasoning stays verbal. Supply or directly teach any contextual information not already in the course.
paragraphs.boundary: The earlier proposal cites a 2022 VWO-I Importheffing task as a possible target-design input. Carry that reference forward for later source verification, not as a completed adaptation or evidence that every operation is approved. Later current-account and game-theory demands stay outside this chapter. Claims about protected jobs do not require or establish a formal economy-wide employment result.
